title: The August Crossword: First Words
dek: 18 words this issue keeps using, fitted into one grid. Solve it out loud with a partner and you have rehearsed half the vocabulary of the month.

blocks.text: Every word in this grid comes from the pages around it: the classroom in the photographs, the first minute of a lesson, the courage it takes to say the wrong thing out loud, one breakfast from the Culinary Salon. Solve it with a pen and a partner — one reads the clue, the other says the answer first.

**How to solve it aloud.** Read the clue in the language you are learning. Say the answer out loud before you write a letter. If you are stuck, say the first sound and let your partner finish the word. The grid rewards the people who speak first and write second.

blocks.title: This could be a good research question
blocks.content: Does solving a crossword aloud, with a partner, move a word into active use faster than copying it into a notebook? Run it for two weeks with your speaking club: half the group copies ten words, half solves the puzzle aloud, then both groups use the words in a five-minute conversation. Count how many each group actually says.

blocks.text: One last instruction for the classroom: do not hand out the key. Read the answers aloud, one number at a time, and ask the group to mark their own grid. The correction is the lesson.
